A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRADIEND study of German definite articles. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across six language models, including encoded-feature correlations, intervention effects, parameter overlaps, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds dem–des transition results and a manual assessment of dataset annotation quality.

M1.justification: The GRADIEND architecture, alternative-gradient inputs, gradient-difference targets, identity pairs, reconstruction loss, parameter updates, and decoder-only article heads remain unchanged. The additional transition variants apply the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds direct genitive–dative transitions for masculine and neuter articles, introducing dem–des transition coverage in Tables 2–3 and Appendix D. The underlying corpora, twelve gender–case datasets, language, and downstream benchmark remain the same.

E2.justification: The same six language models and comparisons between original and GRADIEND-modified models are retained. No competing method or baseline is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1.4 introduces a manual audit of 20 randomly sampled texts from each of twelve datasets. Text accuracy requires every mask to be correctly labeled, while confusion matrices count individual masks. Existing splits, training settings, and the 99% language-modeling preservation constraint remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused annotation-error analysis, reporting cell accuracies and five surface-form confusion matrices that distinguish incorrect gender–case assignments from other token uses. The existing pooling-length, disjoint-article control, and Top-k sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three training seeds with validation-based selection, permutation tests, Cohen's d, FDR correction, and bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals. The new annotation audit adds descriptive results without introducing uncertainty estimates or a new repeated-run practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds dem–des correlations, encoded-value distributions, and overlap results, including an 80.4% mean overlap in Table 5. The new audit reports overall accuracy of 0.83 in Table 7, although Section 7 says 82%. Existing intervention results in Table 4 and v1 Table 9/v2 Table 15 are unchanged; reordered correlation columns also retain their values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for transitions, gradients, reconstruction, probability changes, intervention selection, and parameter overlap are retained. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: Both versions argue against a strictly rule-based account of German article behavior and infer partial reliance on memorized associations from intervention spillover and shared parameters. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain this claim and scope.

C2.justification: v1 only acknowledges possible annotation noise. v2 distinguishes potentially systematic gender–case confusions, especially for des, from errors interpreted as random noise, and argues that consistent findings across cleaner and noisier dataset combinations reduce concern about this confound.

D1.justification: v2 documents the manual-label criteria and the distinction between text-level accuracy and mask-level confusion counts. Table 6 replaces abbreviated dataset IDs with descriptive identifiers, and the Wikipedia source link changes namespace while retaining the stated snapshot. Existing checkpoints, hyperparameters, hardware, and release information remain.

R1.justification: Section 7 newly connects the noise-tolerance argument to earlier GRADIEND findings involving race and religion. The cited-work set and broader positioning remain stable; the GRADIEND reference's change from a 2025 preprint to a 2026 conference publication is a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introduction and methodology with a counterfactual explanation and an overview of the three analyses, adds Appendix A.1.4, and refines some terminology and wording. Most prose and the section hierarchy remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains an architecture-and-analysis overview, transition tables gain grouping labels and additional columns, and the audit introduces accuracy and confusion tables. Two encoded-value figures and additional overlap panels are added. Existing displays are also enlarged or relocated within the retained two-column layout.

improvement.justification: The manual audit quantifies annotation noise previously only acknowledged, and the expanded overview makes the method easier to follow. Added transition results modestly extend coverage. These gains are limited by the audit's small samples, its 82% versus 83% discrepancy, and apparent row-label errors in Tables 8 and 10; the central findings and methodological limitations remain.
